principles.fact: An area counts as outdoor when at least 30% of its perimeter is permanently open. A partial cover traps a 'heat cloud' that adds a convective boost.
Radiant (infrared) heat warms people and objects, not air, so it works in light wind; forced air does not work outdoors and outdoor heat cannot be thermostatically controlled.
Short wave ≈90% radiant, warms instantly; medium wave ≈60% radiant, ≈30 s warm-up; long wave ≈40% radiant, ≈5 min warm-up, most wind-sensitive.
US electric heaters follow ANSI/NFPA 70 (NEC); Bromic guidance: wall mounts at least 72" above floor, ceiling mounts at least 96" (varies with output). Check with the local building authority.
US gas heaters follow ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54. Certification marks: Intertek, UL, CSA. Check with the local building authority.
Electric: recess kits, suspension poles. Gas: heat deflectors (dual-layer stainless, reduce top clearance), ceiling poles (two units back to back).
Complimentary design service: heater selection, placement, coverage drawings from photos, plans or drawings. bromic.com/design-your-space/ · 1-800-301-1293 (Mon–Fri 9–4 PT).
